"""Date ranges, see SPEC.md."""
import calendar
import datetime
import re

_FULL_DATE = re.compile(r"([0-9]{4})-([0-9]{2})-([0-9]{2})")
_YEAR_MONTH = re.compile(r"([0-9]{4})-([0-9]{2})")
_ISO_WEEK = re.compile(r"([0-9]{4})-W([0-9]{2})")
_YEAR = re.compile(r"([0-9]{4})")


def _term(text):
    """Return the inclusive ``(first, last)`` day pair of one date term.

    A full ISO date covers itself, a month covers the whole month, an ISO week
    covers Monday to Sunday and a year covers the whole year. Anything else
    raises ``ValueError``.
    """
    match = _FULL_DATE.fullmatch(text)
    if match:
        day = datetime.date(int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2)), int(match.group(3)))
        return day, day

    match = _YEAR_MONTH.fullmatch(text)
    if match:
        first = datetime.date(int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2)), 1)
        length = calendar.monthrange(first.year, first.month)[1]
        return first, first + datetime.timedelta(days=length - 1)

    match = _ISO_WEEK.fullmatch(text)
    if match:
        monday = datetime.date.fromisocalendar(int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2)), 1)
        return monday, monday + datetime.timedelta(days=6)

    match = _YEAR.fullmatch(text)
    if match:
        year = int(match.group(1))
        return datetime.date(year, 1, 1), datetime.date(year, 12, 31)

    raise ValueError(f"not a date, month, ISO week or year: {text!r}")


def parse_range(text):
    """Parse ``text`` into an inclusive ``(start, end)`` pair of dates.

    ``A..B`` spans from the first day of A to the last day of B; either side
    may be left open. A lone term is its own span, so ``"2026-10"`` is the
    whole month. Errors raise ``ValueError``.
    """
    stripped = text.strip()
    head, separator, tail = stripped.partition("..")
    if not separator:
        return _term(stripped)

    head, tail = head.strip(), tail.strip()
    if not head and not tail:
        raise ValueError(f"both ends of the range are open: {text!r}")

    start = _term(head)[0] if head else None
    end = _term(tail)[1] if tail else None
    if start is not None and end is not None and start > end:
        raise ValueError(f"range ends before it starts: {text!r}")
    return start, end
